bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme as deterministic evidence-package representation contract
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Static inspection of exactly the official RFC Editor RFC 8785 source in this invocation, following p1-sa-551. No implementation, second public source, runtime execution, external service, or protected/manual execution was consumed.
observations: RFC 8785 explicitly defines a canonical JSON representation intended to make hashing/signing reliably repeatable, using strict primitive serialization, I-JSON constraints, deterministic recursive property sorting, no emitted inter-token whitespace, and final UTF-8 encoding.

The input contract forbids duplicate property names, requires Unicode strings and IEEE-754-double-expressible numeric data, and requires parsed JSON strings to remain unchanged; JCS does not apply Unicode normalization.
Object properties are recursively sorted by raw property-name UTF-16 code units; arrays preserve element order while contained objects are recursively sorted.
The final result is a platform-independent UTF-8 byte representation intended to be usable as cryptographic-method input.

RFC 8785 does not itself define an evidence provenance envelope, source/version identity binding, observation-versus-inference-versus-uncertainty fields, replay transcript, checkpoint/continuation schema, content hash field, or persistence transport.
bounded_slice.inference: RFC 8785 supplies the previously missing deterministic canonical-representation contract for JSON evidence packages within its I-JSON/IEEE-754 scope. It therefore closes the representation-ambiguity subproblem identified in p1-sa-551, but it is not a standalone replay-complete evidence handoff: provenance, source identity/version, observation/inference/uncertainty separation, integrity binding, replay instructions, and continuation still require an explicit envelope. Applying JCS to arbitrary package instances also requires a conforming canonicalization implementation or an equivalently verified transformation; no such execution path was tested in this slice.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: No claim is made about conformance, availability, cost, quota behavior, or correctness of any JCS implementation, nor about non-I-JSON data, higher-precision numeric encodings, cryptographic hashing/signing, or a complete replay-envelope design because those surfaces were not tested.
bounded_slice.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_us: No richer-mode/protected/manual step is inherent to the RFC specification, but a conforming canonicalization execution path for arbitrary package instances remains unverified and therefore unresolved rather than accepted.
bounded_slice.quota_zero_assessment: The RFC-defined representation contract itself has no paid/monthly hosted quota or credit dependency and no incremental monetary cost. This does not establish quota-zero execution for any implementation because none was tested.
bounded_slice.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: only frozen sanitized controls, own role-local p1-sa-551/LATEST state, and one official public primary source were semantically consumed; no O/O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, protected-primary, manual-user, or scheduler semantic input was used.

continuation: Next invocation re-bootstrap/freeze authority, reconstruct p1-sa-552, then inspect exactly one official primary source for a self-describing provenance/integrity envelope standard compatible with canonical JSON (prefer W3C PROV-O/PROV-DM or an IETF content-digest specification, choosing only one source) to test the next missing replay-package field set; checkpoint only that one-source observation and retain JCS application/executor verification as an unresolved child, with no second source or execution step.
